title: Funerals, baptisms and brass bands in Donaldsonville compared with New Orleans
summary: Donaldsonville funerals had brass bands but less second line than New Orleans; he describes baptism processions with humming to the river and the family's move around 1915.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: What about the funerals out there? Are they similar to the funerals here with brass bands?

Well, yes. Raybone had one of the famous brass bands. They'd had, like we had in New Orleans, I mean like when they'd have a funeral, the brass band would play. Now they didn't have so much second line like we had. They had some of it and then they would play a kind of jazz tune coming back, you see. But I wouldn't say it was glamorous as New Orleans was, you know. They didn't do it that way so much. And then I remember when I was a kid and I think it was the Baptist and Methodist they used to have where they'd be going to the river for baptism. And you could hear a man humming for the start, seemingly it starts some way out from the program, about the tracks. And you could hear that big gathering in the street humming and singing if you're going to the river, you see. Yeah. And that was something I'd always picture as a kid. I remember well, I said it and it always had that rhythm and beat to the songs, you know. Everybody would be shouting and praying on the way and everything. And what I want to say, we moved out of Downsville, I'd say about 1915. And we moved up on Boedate and Oak, Boedate and Oak I remember very well. I was seemingly, I must have been about seven or eight years old then.
